fastkcv

Fast, exact cross-validation for global kriging, as a companion to gstat. kcv() takes the same inputs as gstat::krige.cv() and returns the same output. It factorizes the covariance matrix of the observations once, instead of refitting the kriging system for every fold, and the results agree with krige.cv() to numerical precision. A covariance matrix too ill-conditioned for that (typically a Gaussian model without a nugget) gives a warning.

  • Leave-one-out, k-fold and buffered (spatial) leave-one-out cross-validation for simple, ordinary and universal kriging.
  • gstat variogram models Nug, Exp, Sph, Gau, Mat, Ste, Cir, Pen, Bes, Wav and Hol, nested sums of them and 2D geometric anisotropy. data.frame, sf and sp data.
  • Random, spatial block and k-means fold builders, and kcv_metrics() to compare fold designs (RMSE, bias, z-scores, interval coverage).
  • Several responses at the same locations (cbind(z1, z2) ~ 1, or kcv_run(prepared, y = )) cross-validated from one factorization.
  • kcv_prepare() / kcv_run() to factorize once and run many fold schemes; kcv_engine() for a precomputed covariance matrix.

Installation

Using remotes:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("n-c-taylor/fastkcv", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Using pak (faster):

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("n-c-taylor/fastkcv")

The package contains C++ code, so installing from GitHub needs a compiler toolchain: Rtools on Windows, the Xcode command line tools on macOS.

Example 

library(fastkcv)
library(gstat)
data(meuse, package = "sp")
v <- vgm(0.59, "Sph", 897, 0.05)

# Leave-one-out, as krige.cv(log(zinc) ~ 1, ~ x + y, meuse, model = v)
cv <- kcv(log(zinc) ~ 1, ~ x + y, meuse, model = v)
kcv_metrics(cv)

# One factorization, several fold designs
p <- kcv_prepare(log(zinc) ~ sqrt(dist), ~ x + y, meuse, model = v)
set.seed(1)
kcv_metrics(kcv_run(p, folds = fold_random(~ x + y, meuse, k = 10)))
kcv_metrics(kcv_run(p, folds = fold_blocks(~ x + y, meuse, blocks = 3)))
kcv_metrics(kcv_run(p, buffer = 300))

Performance

Ordinary kriging on simulated data, 4-core laptop with OpenBLAS (median seconds; from the scripts in inst/bench/):

n LOO: fastkcv / krige.cv() 5-fold: fastkcv / krige.cv()
1,000 0.06 / 67 (1,100x) 0.07 / 0.8 (12x)
2,000 0.25 / 368 (1,500x) 0.29 / 5.7 (19x)
5,000 2.1 / not run 2.6 / 85 (32x)

The gain is largest for leave-one-out and smallest for a few large folds. kcv() handles n = 20,000 in about two minutes.

The vignette (vignette("fastkcv")) covers the fold designs, buffered leave-one-out, precomputed covariance matrices, and the performance and memory notes.

Scope

Global kriging only: every observation is in the kriging neighborhood. Local neighborhoods (nmax, nmin, maxdist), block kriging, unbounded variograms, geographic coordinates and re-fitting the variogram in each fold are not supported, and give an error. Memory is one n x n matrix (8 n^2 bytes, 3.2 GB at n = 20,000), checked before anything is allocated.

Related packages

fastkcv is a companion to gstat, not a fork or a replacement: kcv() takes the inputs of krige.cv() and returns its output, and fitting variograms and kriging new locations stay with gstat. DiceKriging and spmodel also compute exact closed-form cross-validation, for their own models and inputs; blockCV and spatialsample build spatial folds that can be passed to kcv_run(folds = ). The vignette’s section “Related packages” compares them in detail. spmodel also exports a function kcv(): with both attached, call fastkcv::kcv().

Use of AI tools

This package was developed with the help of an AI coding assistant (Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5), used for writing and reviewing code, tests and documentation. The author directed the work and is responsible for the package; its results are checked against gstat::krige.cv() and independent R implementations by the test suite.
